title: Shutdown, Day 43
text: A deputy walks you through the longest shutdown in history, one agency at a time. Nobody mentions a ballroom.

options.label: Sit through the whole slide deck
options.result: The lights come back on in the agencies. Your name was on one slide, in the footnotes.

ignore.text: The shutdown is now older than some sandwiches in the White House fridge.

inspiredBy: The record-long federal shutdown of October-November 2025.

title: The Rehiring Ledger
text: A personnel officer presents a spreadsheet of workers fired in February and rehired in March. Some were rehired by the same person who fired them.

options.label: Read every row aloud, slowly
options.result: The ledger balances, in the sense that nobody can find the first column.

ignore.text: Fired staff keep getting hired back by e-mail. Nobody is sure who is on the payroll, including payroll.

inspiredBy: Agencies rehiring workers laid off in the 2025 efficiency drive, including nuclear weapons staff fired and rehired within a day.

title: The Acting Org Chart
text: A flowchart shows one official acting as head of three agencies, plus a fourth on Thursdays. The arrows are circular.

options.label: Learn who is acting what
options.result: You now know who is in charge of what. By Friday it will be different.

ignore.text: A single official signs the memo, countersigns it, and then appeals it to himself.

inspiredBy: Officials holding several top posts at once in 2025, including a cabinet member running more than one agency.

title: Watchdog Vacancies
text: A clerk reads out the list of agencies whose inspector general posts are filled by deputies, acting deputies and, in one case, a very tall plant.

options.label: Hear the full roll call
options.result: The posts are tallied. The plant has the best attendance record.

ignore.text: Seventeen offices have nobody asking awkward questions. Honestly, it is a little eerie.

inspiredBy: The mass firing of about 17 inspectors general in January 2025 and the acting replacements.

title: How Jobs Are Counted
text: Statisticians explain survey response rates and why last month's figure was revised. You ask whether the figure can be revised to be better.

options.label: Accept that revisions are routine
options.result: It turns out numbers get adjusted as more data arrives. You were visibly let down.

ignore.text: The job numbers arrive late, then change, then change back. Markets do not like your face.

inspiredBy: The August 2025 firing of the labor statistics chief after large downward jobs revisions.

title: Controller Workforce Plan
text: The aviation agency presents a plan to hire thousands of controllers. Training takes years. You ask for it by Thursday.

options.label: Absorb the training timeline
options.result: The plan is sound. It will help in roughly the next presidency.

ignore.text: Tower staff are on overtime and snacks. A departure board has simply given up.

inspiredBy: The 2025-26 push to hire thousands of air traffic controllers amid shortages and shutdown delays.

title: Ranger Headcount
text: A parks official unrolls a map. The dots are rangers. There are very few dots, and one of them is a bear in a ranger hat.

options.label: Study the map in silence
options.result: You approve more seasonal rangers. The bear is not reappointed.

ignore.text: Visitor centers are staffed by a laminated sign saying Back in 15 Minutes. It is year-round.

inspiredBy: National Park Service staffing cuts and partial reinstatements in 2025.

title: Lease Termination Review
text: A real estate officer reviews hundreds of building leases that were canceled, uncanceled and canceled again. Some offices were still full of people.

options.label: Initial each page
options.result: Over 480 leases are spared. The building you wanted gilded is not among them.

ignore.text: A department is evicted from its own office and holds its meetings on the steps.

inspiredBy: The 2025 efficiency drive terminated hundreds of federal leases, many later spared.

title: Federal Records Briefing
text: An archivist explains that official messages must be kept, even the ones with a thumbs-up emoji, even the ones that disappear on purpose.

options.label: Learn the retention rules
options.result: Everyone agrees to keep records. The chat app agrees to disagree.

ignore.text: The archive request arrives for a chat nobody remembers, and it is somehow the one you were in.

inspiredBy: Lawsuits and FOIA reports in 2025 on cabinet use of auto-deleting messaging apps for official business.

title: A Commissioner Needed
text: The statistics bureau needs a new head. Your shortlist is one economist and one friend who is very good at saying numbers are great.

options.label: Appoint the veteran economist
options.result: The numbers keep arriving as numbers. This is considered suspicious by people who like better ones.

options.label: Appoint the numbers cheerleader
options.result: Every month is the best month ever. Economists begin laughing in a measured, quarterly way.

ignore.text: The bureau is run by an acting deputy who is just trying to do arithmetic.

inspiredBy: Turmoil at the labor statistics bureau after the August 2025 firing of its commissioner.

title: A Dismal Report
text: The jobs report is weak. An adviser suggests publishing it unchanged. Another suggests it was obviously written by someone unfriendly.

options.label: Publish and explain the context
options.result: The report is released with caveats. The caveats are the most popular part.

options.label: Declare the numbers rigged
options.result: The numbers are now rigged by decree. The actual numbers are unimpressed and arrive anyway.

ignore.text: The report speaks for itself, and it is not flattering.

inspiredBy: The 2025 weak jobs report and the claim by the White House that the figures were rigged.

title: The Watchdog Report
text: An inspector general has found a spending problem at an agency you like. The report is 200 pages and has a very small font.

options.label: Let the review proceed
options.result: The report is published. Your agency promises to take the 200 pages seriously.

options.label: Replace the inspector general
options.result: The inspector general is replaced. The problems are not. The new one does not read small fonts.

ignore.text: The report sits unread, where all the best reports sit.

inspiredBy: Firings and replacements of inspectors general in 2025.

title: Another Efficiency Cut
text: The efficiency czar wants to eliminate a whole agency by Friday. Asked what it does, he says it has too many letters.

options.label: Study what the agency does first
options.result: A review finds the agency inspects things that explode. It is kept.

options.label: Cut it, and cut a ribbon too
options.result: The agency is gone on Friday and rehired on Saturday. The ribbon remains in place.

ignore.text: Half the agency is fired, half rehired, and nobody can say which half.

inspiredBy: The 2025 efficiency drive that cut agencies, then rehired staff when services broke.

title: Forecasters Needed
text: The weather service lost hundreds of staff and needs to hire meteorologists back. Meanwhile the forecast for your approval is cloudy.

options.label: Approve the rehiring
options.result: Forecasters return. It is going to rain, and for once somebody was warned.

options.label: Rename the forecast after yourself
options.result: The Presidential Weather is now partly sunny with a chance of statues. Pilots are baffled.

ignore.text: The forecast is a man looking out of a window, with a tablet.

inspiredBy: The National Weather Service losing over 560 staff in 2025 then getting approval to rehire about 125.

title: A Postal Proposal
text: An adviser proposes moving the postal service under a cabinet department. The postal service points out that it has delivered mail since 1775.

options.label: Leave the mail alone
options.result: The mail continues to arrive. A letter carrier salutes you, and you have no idea why.

options.label: Put your face on the stamp
options.result: The stamp is issued, then sticks to every envelope, and to your hands.

ignore.text: The postal service stays in limbo, and so do four birthday cards.

inspiredBy: 2025 reports of White House interest in changing the postal service's governance and finances.

title: The Park Pass Design
text: A new annual pass for national parks needs a picture on the front. Options are a mountain, a bison, or a very handsome president.

options.label: Print the mountain
options.result: The mountain is chosen. It is more photogenic than you, and it knows it.

options.label: Print your portrait, huge
options.result: The pass is a bestseller. Wildlife refuses to scan it.

ignore.text: The pass is a plain card, and the bison look bored.

inspiredBy: 2025 reports of changes to national park passes, including pricing and presidential imagery.

title: The Tower Upgrade
text: The aviation agency wants funds to modernize its radar and training. A prominent donor wants the main tower named after you instead.

options.label: Fund the radar and training
options.result: The radar is modernized. It is named the Radar. Nobody cheers.

options.label: Fund a golden tower name sign
options.result: A huge sign goes up, and the radar remains from 1987.

ignore.text: Planes are arriving, by faith and by luck.

inspiredBy: The 2025-26 effort to modernize air traffic control systems amid controller shortages.

title: A Fourth Hat
text: One loyal official already runs two agencies and a security council. You are asked whether to give him a third agency, as a treat.

options.label: Name a separate person
options.result: A new person is hired. The first official finally gets to sit down.

options.label: Add a fourth job to his pile
options.result: He now chairs a meeting of himself. It runs long and the minutes are signed twice.

ignore.text: The official signs the same memo as three different titles.

inspiredBy: One official holding multiple top posts at once in 2025, including a cabinet member as acting head of other agencies.

title: The Group Chat
text: Staff want to coordinate strikes on a messaging app. Security says use the secure system. The app has better emoji and a thumbs-up for you.

options.label: Use the secure room
options.result: Everyone moves to the secure room. It has no emoji, and it has no reporters.

options.label: Add you to a bigger chat
options.result: The chat grows to fifty. A reporter joins as plus one.

ignore.text: Plans are texted in public, with a handshake emoji.

inspiredBy: The March 2025 group chat leak in which a journalist was added to a chat about military strikes.

title: The Loyalty Quiz
text: An agency head wants to hire by merit. A deputy wants to include a quiz asking how much you won the election by. The answer key is you.

options.label: Hire on skills and merit
options.result: Qualified candidates are hired. All of them do not know your favorite font.

options.label: Add the quiz for new hires
options.result: Everyone passes. The agency now runs on affirmation and dread.

ignore.text: Hiring stalls as nobody can agree on the quiz.

inspiredBy: 2025 efforts to reclassify civil service jobs and prioritize loyalty in federal hiring.

title: The Fork in the Road
text: Staff are offered a deferred resignation by one email with the subject line a fork. A unit wants to know if it can be less cryptic.

options.label: Send a clear, polite notice
options.result: The notice is clear. It uses the word please, twice. It is a little unsettling.

options.label: Send a second, fork-themed email
options.result: The second email contains a spoon. Staff are no clearer on the matter.

ignore.text: Employees receive one more email, and then another, and then silence.

inspiredBy: The January 2025 deferred resignation email offered to federal workers.

title: Shutdown Press Conference
text: Reporters ask when the shutdown ends and whose fault it is. You want to discuss the ballroom.

options.label: Explain the funding deal
options.result: You explain a spending bill, fully. Reporters write that you seemed genuinely bored by it.

options.label: Blame everyone, brag about gold
options.result: You blame four parties and a ghost. The ballroom gets a single, golden mention.

ignore.text: The podium is surrounded by empty chairs and frozen microphones.

inspiredBy: The October-November 2025 shutdown and the White House messaging around it.

title: The Cabinet Meeting Cameras
text: A televised cabinet meeting. Each member is expected to open with praise for you. One is running late, and one has fallen asleep.

options.label: Move straight to the agenda
options.result: The meeting is over in forty minutes. Praise is limited to a quick nod.

options.label: Run the praise round, fully
options.result: The meeting runs three hours. By the end, you have been compared to a sunrise.

ignore.text: The cabinet meeting runs long, with no agenda, and no snacks.

inspiredBy: The 2025 televised cabinet meetings featuring long sessions of praise for the president.

title: The Turnover Question
text: A reporter asks why so many senior aides have departed this year. It is a long list. It is read aloud, and the reporter runs out of breath.

options.label: Credit the staff who stayed
options.result: You thank the survivors. They look, with some dignity, like survivors.

options.label: Say everyone left for a promotion
options.result: Many have been promoted to unemployment. The reporter asks a very polite follow-up.

ignore.text: The list is read in full, and the room applauds the reader's lungs.

inspiredBy: High turnover of senior White House and cabinet staff in 2025 and 2026.

title: The Efficiency Farewell
text: The efficiency czar is leaving. Reporters ask what he saved. He holds up a chainsaw and a very long slide.

options.label: Thank him and give real totals
options.result: The real savings are shown. They are smaller than the slide, and smaller than the chainsaw.

options.label: Hand him a trophy and a gold chainsaw
options.result: The trophy is presented. It cost more than what was saved that day.

ignore.text: The czar leaves quietly, apart from a faint chainsaw sound.

inspiredBy: The departure of the lead of the 2025 efficiency drive and disputes over claimed savings.

title: Call From Transport
text: The transportation secretary reports that controllers are working overtime and that a runway is, technically, a parking lot. He wants an update.

options.label: Authorize hiring and training
options.result: Hiring is authorized. The secretary hangs up happily, and a bit surprised.

options.label: Ask if the tower sign can be gold
options.result: The secretary says no, politely. Then he says it a few more times.

ignore.text: Delays pile up like luggage, and nobody can find the carousel.

inspiredBy: Transportation officials' warnings in 2025 of controller shortages and delays during the shutdown.

title: Call From the Mail
text: The postmaster general reports that the post office is losing money but also delivering the mail. He says it is difficult to do both.

options.label: Offer a modest funding plan
options.result: A modest plan is agreed. The postmaster says thanks, and the stamps keep coming.

options.label: Suggest selling the mail to a friend
options.result: The friend declines. He says he already has a lot of packages.

ignore.text: The postal service waits for instructions, which arrive slightly late.

inspiredBy: Reports in 2025 on postal service finances and proposals to change its governance.

title: Call From Interior
text: The interior secretary reports that parks are short of staff and one geyser is not doing its job. He wants to rehire seasonal rangers.

options.label: Approve the seasonal hires
options.result: Rangers are rehired. The geyser, for its part, returns to work too.

options.label: Ask for a geyser named after you
options.result: The geyser is renamed. It now erupts only when someone says your name.

ignore.text: The geyser is unsupervised, and has never been happier.

inspiredBy: National park staffing shortages and reinstatements in 2025.

title: Call From a Governor
text: A governor says food aid payments are delayed by the shutdown and asks you to help. The governor has a map, and a very short fuse.

options.label: Back a quick funding fix
options.result: Funds flow, and the governor thanks you in a tone like a snow shovel.

options.label: Say it is all someone else's doing
options.result: You blame three people. The governor calls it a regional record.

ignore.text: The governor keeps calling, and the line holds on a theme tune.

inspiredBy: State officials' pleas about delayed aid during the 2025 shutdown.

title: Call From Your Chief of Staff
text: Your chief of staff has screened all calls and meetings for your own good. She says you should do fewer things at once. You disagree.

options.label: Accept her revised schedule
options.result: Your day is now organized, and this, she says, is the point.

options.label: Overrule her and fire the schedule
options.result: The schedule is gone. By lunch you are in three meetings and no one knows which.

ignore.text: The calendar fills with lunches, and with a man you never invited.

inspiredBy: Tension and turnover around White House chiefs of staff and schedulers, reported 2025.
